answers.rationale: For trail/recovery weekends, she repeatedly favors a lodge near the activity when it confirms coffee/fridge and has pool, hot tub, and fitness access, accepting less downtown dining convenience. Mountain Base Lodge preserves that recovery bundle and room reliability while remaining only 10-12 minutes from the clinics. Ski Resort Tower adds a substantial premium and airport-route detour; Downtown House and College Inn give up the pool/hot-tub recovery setup.

Her work-trip pattern is to reject unclear room basics, while treating a short, dependable hospital commute as more important than chasing a hot tub. Medical Center Suites supplies the confirmed queen-suite routine, fridge, coffee, fitness, and pool, while staying close enough for badge pickup and the supply cart. Campus Guesthouse has double-bed and fridge/coffee caveats; Westroads adds a materially longer morning drive mainly for the hot tub; Midtown gives up the pool without improving the hospital logistics.

The 12:45 nonstop is genuinely brittle after an 11:50 finish, but the 2:15 departure leaves roughly 2 hours and 25 minutes before departure with no presenter materials to retrieve and only a 25-minute airport trip. That is the kind of adequate same-day buffer she has accepted, and the 75-minute connection is not unusually short relative to connections she has accepted. It gets her home an hour before the much later nonstop, without the unnecessary Monday hotel night.

In repeated conference ties, she has led with the nearby suite that confirms a queen room, in-room coffee, and refrigerator rather than a more convenient block room where the fridge is only a request. She has accepted a short rideshare for early presenter mornings in exchange for that dependable room routine. The suite hotel therefore fits better than the six-minute-walk block hotel with request-only refrigerator inventory; the airport Hampton and boutique both weaken the in-room coffee/fridge setup.
